column3: ACP snapshot suite entry point: maps the nine scenario snapshot.yml manifests onto Scenario descriptors (header pin, sidecar sources, permission env, platform, configPath) and calls defineAcpSnapshotSuite with the shipped dsh CLI as agent-under-test.
Controller script: initialize -> newSession -> promptAndCancel gated on the tool-written marker started.txt -> waitForTurnEnd; forces a cancel while one bash call runs and a second is queued.
Authored model script: two bash tool calls (call_wait writes started.tmp then renames to started.txt and spins; call_skipped writes skipped.txt), plus usage and finish{tool-calls} chunks.
V2 recording (20 events): tool results are role:user messages with a nested tool-result block; two distinct abort codes ABORTED (killed) and ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH (never started); no job events.
V3 recording (21 events): adds the system/message node and sections on the runtime-context message; tool-result nesting unchanged; sourceEventSeqs recomputed for the new sequence.

V4 recording (23 events): adds job/registered and job/settled (status killed, cause kill, detail 'signal: SIGTERM; tool call aborted') and promotes tool results to role:tool with top-level toolCallId; the queued call gets no job events.
Ownership manifest: composition acp-default, recording authored (never re-recorded), replay.override true, platform posix (bash semantics), workspace.final true (complete final-state oracle).
ACP transcript oracle: both tool calls surface as in_progress then fail with distinct texts ('tool call aborted' vs 'tool call aborted before dispatch'), then result{stopReason:'cancelled'}.
Independent external-effect oracle: the file the cancelled bash tool really created; its presence plus the absence of skipped.txt is the assertion.
Controller script: promptAndCancel gated on the .dsh-snapshot-stream-ready marker file, then waitForTurnEnd; the cancel is deterministic because it waits on a filesystem signal, not a timer.
One-element replay override [{kind:'hang', readyFile:'.dsh-snapshot-stream-ready'}]: the model adapter pretends to stream forever and writes the marker the controller waits on.

V2 recording (16 events): system prompt lives inside request/header as {{system}}, no system/message event; abort reason is the nested union {kind:'aborted',reason:{kind:'user'}}; assistant message carries interrupted:true with a partial text-chunks row.

V3 recording (17 events): system prompt promoted to a real system/message node with source {kind:'plugin',plugin:'@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt'}; runtime-context message carries named sections; request/header keeps only config+tools.

V4 recording (17 events): message provenance becomes semantic kinds (system-prompt, runtime-context) and the runtime context gains a working-directory:current section; the compressed stream row keeps per-token dt timing.
Ownership manifest: composition acp-default, recording authored (a live model cannot be coaxed into a deterministic cancel), replay.override true, header.class acp-default with no pin.
ACP transcript oracle: initialize capability frame, newSession configOptions select, one agent_message_chunk with 'partial', then result{stopReason:'cancelled'} - a cancelled turn is not silent.

Replay-only patch layered over cordis.yml: disables the live LLM adapter, inserts dsh-llm-replay with the same provider/model ids, keeps persistence uncompressed, and inserts the shell-path plugin that rewrites the one recorded /tmp path; the rest of the plugin stack stays real.

Live composition patch: llm-deepseek (thinking enabled, reasoningEffort max), sandbox-policy and approval policy both derived from DSH_PERMISSION_MODE via YAML js tags, zstd persistence live vs none under DSH_SNAPSHOT, persona prefix teaching that a sandbox denial is policy, subagent spawn+fork at maxDepth 1, and session-log disabled so stdout stays pure ACP JSON-RPC.

Controller script: one directive prompt naming the exact command, sandbox_permissions and justification, ending with 'reply with the single word DONE'; permissionAnswers allow_once selects by option kind because option ids are agent-issued randoms.

V2 recording (23 events): approval/asked carries the escalation reason, approval/decided outcome allowed-once, tool result is role:user with a nested tool-result block; step 2 shows cacheReadTokens 1664 vs inputTokens 27.

V3 recording (24 events): adds the system/message node and drops system from request/header, isolating one format change; reasoning is its own content block streamed as reasoning-chunks with per-token dt.

V4 recording (26 events): job/registered + job/settled (status completed, cause producer, detail 'exit code: 0'), role:tool result with meta.cwd, and step-2 usage showing inputTokens 27 against cacheReadTokens 1664 - the prompt-prefix cache hit.
Ownership manifest and sole header pin for class acp-default: recording live, pin true, systemPromptSource and toolSchemasSource both session/text-turn, permission workspace-write.

ACP transcript oracle: reasoning as agent_thought_chunk, tool_call in_progress with rawInput showing sandbox_permissions and justification, a server-initiated session/request_permission with allow-once/reject-once options, tool_call_update completed, then DONE and stopReason end_turn.
Scenario-local Cordis plugin: on 'subagent/end' writes an empty .dsh-snapshot-subagent-settled marker into the cwd, because child progress has no ACP update to wait on.
Git symlink (mode 120000) to ../../session/text-turn/system-prompt.expected.md; the readable prompt body lives in one place and is borrowed through the declared systemPromptSource.
Git symlink (mode 120000) to ../../session/text-turn/tool-schemas.expected.json; the tool-schema set behind the {{tools}} token in request/header, shared by the whole acp-default header class.
Controller script: the exact twin of the approved scenario with the answer flipped to reject_once, and the prompt additionally instructing the model not to retry or work around the denial.

V2 recording (23 events): the denial arrives as a tool result (isError true, text 'the user rejected escalating this command to "danger-full-access"'), not as an exception, and the turn still ends completed.
V3 recording (24 events): adds the system/message node; denial text unchanged from V2; step-2 usage shows the same 1664-token cache read as the approved scenario.

V4 recording (24 events): the denial text is widened to '...it stays denied, so stop and explain instead of working around it', and there are NO job events because a rejected approval never dispatches the tool.
Ownership manifest: class acp-default member with no pin (compared against the escalation-approved pin), recording live, permission workspace-write.

ACP transcript oracle: identical permission-request frame to the approved scenario but the following tool_call_update is status failed and carries the full guidance clause; stopReason is end_turn, not an error.
Controller script: prompt forces the fs write tool (NOT bash) with sandbox_permissions and justification, then permissionAnswers allow_once.
V2 recording (23 events): write tool result carries meta{diffs:[]} only - no operation and no path yet - while the approval reason and the allowed-once outcome are both persisted.
V3 recording (24 events): meta gains operation:'create'; the fs tool set makes step 1 cost 3871 input tokens versus 1501 for the bash scenario.
V4 recording (24 events): meta gains path:'{{cwd}}/escalated.md' alongside operation and diffs; step-2 usage shows cacheReadTokens 3968 against inputTokens 107.
Ownership manifest: recording live, permission workspace-write, workspace.final true - proves the escalation path is shared by the fs tool family, not just bash.

ACP transcript oracle: tool_call{title:'write', rawInput with file_path/content/sandbox_permissions/justification}, the same permission frame as bash, then a completed tool_call_update whose content is a path/type/content triple rather than the file contents.
Independent workspace oracle: the complete final tree of the scenario, containing escalated.md with the single line 'escalated' - byte-identical to the fs-same-mode oracle.
Controller script: deliberately no permissionAnswers, because no permission request may ever be issued; the prompt tells the model to request danger-full-access while the session already holds it.

V3 recording (22 events, no V2 fixture): the tool call records sandbox_permissions:'danger-full-access' and a justification that is not really a justification, and NO approval/asked or approval/decided event is emitted.
V4 recording (22 events): same absence of any approval event - the redundant request simply evaporates and the tool runs under the mode the session already had; meta carries operation/path/diffs.

Ownership manifest: permission danger-full-access (so the approval policy resolves to never), recording authored, workspace.final true - pins the negative case that a same-mode request must raise no prompt.

ACP transcript oracle: the escalation transcript minus the session/request_permission frame, yet rawInput still shows sandbox_permissions and justification - the request is recorded even though it was not honoured.
Independent workspace oracle for the same-mode scenario; identical content and blob hash to the fs-escalation-approved oracle, so the only difference between the two scenarios is the approval.
Two-step controller script (initialize, newSession) - no prompt, so the persisted session log holds nothing but its header row.
V2 recording: a single session header line (version 2, id {{session:1}}, createdAt 0, isSeeded false, delegationDepth 0) with no cwd, since the session never ran.
V3 recording: the same one-line header at version 3, byte-identical to the reject-extra-dirs V3 fixture because both scenarios fail before any message is accepted.
Minimal ownership manifest: version/scenario/profile/composition/recording authored/header.class only - no permission, replay, workspace or input section.

ACP capability advertisement: protocolVersion 1, agentInfo, agentCapabilities with sessionCapabilities as a set of empty objects (presence declares the capability), authMethods empty, plus the newSession configOptions model select.

Replay patch for the vision route: live adapter disabled, dsh-llm-replay declaring deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp with inputModalities [text,image], contextWindow 10022 and imageRequestTokens 384, plus the tight compaction budget and the authored summary-image-budget plugin.

Live composition patch selecting the vision model, the durable attachment store, and compaction-basic with headroomTokens 0 / maxTokens 8192 / retainTokens 100 - a budget sized so only route-priced image tokens can trigger the compaction.
Two-turn controller script: promptContent sends six identical 1x1 PNGs interleaved with frame labels, then a second promptContent asks for DONE - pressure comes from image COUNT, not payload size.

V2 recording (29 events): compaction/start then compaction/summary then a checkpoint user/message whose surfaceOp replaces seq 7 - but NO image/offload event, and the checkpoint text and do-not-acknowledge instruction are already present.
V3 recording (31 events): image/offload{targets:[{seq:8,imageIndexes:[0]}]} appears, checkpoint provenance is plugin 'compact', and request/context carries contextWindow 11600.

V4 recording (31 events): full compaction contract - compaction/start, image/offload, compaction/summary with shadowedRange/shadowedTokenCount 366/maxTokens 8192, a checkpoint user/message with source kind 'compact-checkpoint' and surfaceOp replace, then compaction/end.

Ownership manifest with its own header class (image-compaction), pin true, systemPromptSource session/read-image but toolSchemasSource escalation-approved (independent axes), and a content-addressed sha256 attachment declaration.

ACP transcript oracle: promptCapabilities.image is true only here, the model select lists three models, usage_update reports size 10022 (the context window) with a normalized used token, and the compaction itself produces no ACP frame.

Authored fault-injection plugin: intercepts only llm streams with purpose 'compaction' and yields a finish chunk carrying IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED with offloadImages 1, once, so the harness's real image-offload recovery fires deterministically.

Git symlink (mode 120000) to ../../session/read-image/system-prompt.expected.md; the image-compaction scenario borrows its prompt from read-image while borrowing tool schemas from escalation-approved.

Controller script: newSessionExpectError with additionalDirectories ['/extra-dir'] asserts the protocol refusal in both directions - success throws, failure is the expected result and its error frame lands in the transcript.
V2 recording: a one-line session header, byte-identical to the handshake V2 fixture - only the protocol transcript distinguishes the two scenarios.
V3 recording: a one-line session header, byte-identical to the handshake V3 fixture; the corpus tolerates duplicate session-log content even though duplicate sidecar content is rejected.
Ownership manifest for the protocol-refusal scenario: same minimal shape as the handshake, recording authored, no permission or replay section.
ACP transcript oracle: the initialize result followed by a JSON-RPC error frame with the standard invalid-params code -32602 and the message 'Invalid params: additionalDirectories is not supported'.

Normative policy for the whole snapshots tree: normalization fixed points and typed tokens, one readable sidecar owner per header class, generation naming and selection, declared sessionFormat coverage, workspace.expected as an independent oracle, and the ban on adding another application entrypoint or scenario driver.
